title: Identity shadow sync bridge and customer notice protocol
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: Implement a shadow-sync bridging strategy to migrate identities, role assignments, and admin controls from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with dual-write, phased backfill, and structured customer communications. The goal is zero data loss for permissions, full audit log continuity, and measurable convergence with automated reconciliation probes.

Scope:
- Dual-write shim that records changes into RBAC v2 while serving v1 as the authoritative store during canaries.
- Deterministic incremental backfill engine for historical role bindings and org-level policies with idempotency and retry semantics.
- Audit log bridging to ensure every authz decision and mapping change is preserved and correlated across systems.
- SSO/SAML attribute mapping validation and conflict resolution rules (email aliases, external_id, group mappings).
- Admin controls parity (super-admin flags, delegated admin boundaries) and a temporary compatibility layer for console and API.
- Customer-facing comms plan and opt-in/opt-out flow for orgs who want to delay cutover.

Non-goals: full UI redesign of console roles (handled by separate design tickets), long-term RBAC schema evolution post-cutover.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dual-write successfully records >99.9% of authz writes to both stores during canary with no rejects.
- Automated reconciliation reduces divergence to <0.1% by the end of backfill window.
- Audit trail continuity verified for sample of 100K events spanning migration window; no missing parent_event ids.
- SSO mappings for top 10 enterprise customers validated with test asserts; mapping conflicts are auto-tagged and surfaced to customer success.
- Rollback path validated: a staged switchback that resumes v1 authoritative decisions within 10 minutes for failing orgs.

Deliverables:
- Dual-write shim (runtime + telemetry hooks) and feature flag gating.
- Backfill worker with checkpointing, concurrency controls, and rate-limiting per-org.
- Reconciliation dashboard in Console showing per-org divergence, backfill progress, and critical alerts.
- Customer comms templates, opt-in/opt-out APIs, and a runbook for support.
- Cutover runbook with pre-checks, canary cohort definitions, and rollback steps.

Links to artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RBAC/RBAC+v2+Migration+Runbook, https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/tree/migration/dual-write, https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rbac-reconcile (internal demo)

Reconciliation convergence <0.1% divergence after scheduled backfill
Audit continuity validated for representative event set
SSO/SAML mapping verified for top enterprise orgs
Verified rollback resumes v1 authority within 10 minutes

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Divergent role models between v1 and v2 leading to permission gaps - Mitigation: deterministic mapping rules and dry-run policy reports
Risk: SSO attribute collisions - Mitigation: conflict tagging and customer consent flow + manual review by SEs
Risk: Backfill load impacting serving latency - Mitigation: rate-limit backfill, off-peak windows, autoscaling reserved capacity
Risk: Missing audit continuity - Mitigation: forwarder checksum and sample replays during canary
runbook_snippets: Pre-cutover checks: synthetic user flows, reconciliation baseline <0.5%, audit-forwarder heartbeat OK
Canary cohort: 2% of orgs selected by traffic, include 3 enterprise customers with SEs on call
Cutover: enable dual-write -> run backfill -> monitor reconciliation -> flip authoritative flag for cohort
